intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from legendary local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking tour or self-guide using a map of top-rated stalls.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, admiring centuries-old merchant houses, temples, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. Visit during the monthly Lantern Festival when electric lights are turned off and the town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns. Browse the night market for cheap local snacks like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a semi-automatic motorbike and ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, a dramatic mountain road stretching between Da Nang and Hue offering breathtaking coastal views, jungle scenery, and old French and American war bunkers at the summit. A quintessential backpacker experience immortalized by Top Gear.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat & Local Village Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget group day tour from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, hopping on a traditional sampan boat through narrow canals lined with coconut palms. Visit floating markets, a rice paper factory, a coconut candy workshop, and share a home-cooked lunch with a local family, offering deep insight into rural Vietnamese life.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and spend a day exploring the UNESCO-listed Imperial Citadel of Hue, the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty, then pedal out along the Perfume River to visit the ornate royal tombs of Emperor Tu Duc and Minh Mang. Stop at local Banh Khoai stalls along the way for the city's famous crispy pancakes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect baggage, and arrange budget transport (grab taxi or airport bus) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bowl of pho or banh mi from a late-night street stall near the airport if hungry upon arrival (~30,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival day. Keep energy for the days ahead. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs. Avoid overpriced airport taxis — use Grab app for budget-friendly rides.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and explore the beachfront area around the resort on foot. Take a slow morning walk along the beach to get your bearings. Visit a nearby local market to soak in the morning atmosphere and watch vendors set up stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (100,000–150,000 VND/day) and explore the surrounding neighborhood. Visit a nearby pagoda or temple for a taste of Vietnamese spiritual culture. Stroll through local streets and observe daily life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest night market or street food hub. Sample local snacks, interact with vendors, and enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere typical of Vietnamese towns.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi with egg and pate from a street cart (~20,000–30,000 VND) and Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da) (~15,000–20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) from a local rice shop (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food feast at the night market — try bun bo Hue, fresh spring rolls, and grilled corn (~80,000–120,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Get a local SIM card today (Viettel or Vietnamobile, ~100,000 VND for data) to use Grab and Google Maps throughout the trip. Stay hydrated — April can be warm and humid in Vietnam.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby fishing village or harbor early in the morning to watch fishermen return with their catch. This is a quintessential Vietnamese cultural experience. Bring your camera for stunning early light photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local cultural landmark such as a Cham tower, ancient citadel, or heritage museum depending on the specific region. Many such sites have entry fees of only 20,000–50,000 VND for foreigners.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost cultural performance if available locally (check with hostel or resort front desk). Otherwise, relax at a beachside plastic-stool bar with a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass).

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun cha or bun thit nuong (grilled pork noodles) at a local quan (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood skewers and grilled squid from a beach-side street stall (~80,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples or religious sites — cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes before entering pagodas. Bargain respectfully at markets but never aggressively.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby natural attraction — a waterfall, national park, or rice terrace depending on location. Hire a local guide or join a budget group tour (~150,000–300,000 VND) for context and safety.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the natural site. Pack a picnic lunch from local vendors to save money. Swim, hike, or simply enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. Visit a local cooking class or street food tour (~200,000–350,000 VND) to learn how to make pho or fresh spring rolls — a great cultural and culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Pho bo (beef noodle soup) from a local pho shop (~40,000–60,000 VND) — the classic Vietnamese breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed banh mi sandwiches and fruit bought from morning market (~50,000 VND total)
meals.dinner: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class, or grab bun bo Hue from a street stall (~40,000–50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class or food tour the day before if possible. Wear comfortable shoes for any hiking or outdoor activities. Bring insect repellent and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the beach — swim, relax, and enjoy the scenery. This is a good rest morning before a culturally intensive afternoon. Alternatively, try early morning yoga on the beach if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby town's old quarter or heritage street on foot. Look for colonial architecture, local craft shops, and art galleries. Pick up handmade souvenirs directly from artisans to support local economy and get fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop bar or local bia hoi corner and enjoy sunset drinks with locals. Engage in conversation with fellow backpackers or locals — this is the heart of the backpacking experience.

meals.breakfast: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls with pork and mushroom) from a local stall (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork) — a regional specialty (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) shared with fellow travelers at a budget restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hot pot is best enjoyed with a group — great way to bond with other backpackers you meet at the hostel or resort. Try regional specialties unique to the area you're in rather than generic tourist menus.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local wet market (cho) very early (6:00–8:00 AM) to experience the chaotic, colorful, and authentic side of Vietnamese daily commerce. Watch vendors sell fresh produce, meats, and live seafood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day motorbike tour of the surrounding countryside. Ride through rice paddies, small villages, and rural landscapes. This can be self-guided (rent a semi-automatic Honda Wave for ~100,000–150,000 VND/day) or with a local 'Easy Rider' guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and explore a local street food alley after dark. Try lesser-known dishes like banh xeo (sizzling crepes), nem lui (lemongrass skewers), or che (sweet dessert soup).

meals.breakfast: Chao (Vietnamese rice porridge/congee) with century egg or chicken (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com bui (dusty rice) — a local workers' lunch spot serving rice with multiple side dishes (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh xeo (Vietnamese sizzling crepe) wrapped in rice paper with herbs (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a motorbike, ensure you have an International Driving Permit. Always wear a helmet. Avoid riding after dark in unfamiliar areas. Fuel up at local petrol stations (~20,000–25,000 VND per liter).

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget boat trip or kayak tour to explore nearby waterways, mangroves, or islands (~100,000–250,000 VND). Many local fishermen offer informal tours at a fraction of the price of organized tourist boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby island or coastal village accessible by boat. Look for hidden beaches, snorkeling spots, or quiet coves away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cultural event, temple festival, or community gathering if available. Check with locals or your accommodation about any upcoming events. Otherwise, enjoy a quiet evening journaling on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi op la (banh mi with fried eggs) from a cart (~20,000–25,000 VND) with fresh coconut water (~15,000–20,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood grilled on the boat or at a beachside shack — ask for the catch of the day (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) from a local restaurant (~40,000–55,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate boat tour prices before boarding. Going in a group of 2–4 people significantly reduces per-person cost. Bring waterproof bags for electronics during boat trips.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to visiting a significant cultural or historical site in the region — a war museum, royal palace ruins, or ethnic minority village. These offer deep insight into Vietnam's complex history and diverse culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a slow afternoon walk through a local neighborhood away from tourist areas. Pop into a local cafe, practice a few Vietnamese phrases with locals, and observe everyday life at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant for dinner (still budget-friendly by Western standards). Try a multi-course Vietnamese meal with specialty dishes of the region.

meals.breakfast: Hu tieu (southern-style noodle soup) or pho at a local breakfast spot (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh mi thit (pork banh mi) and fresh sugarcane juice (~30,000–40,000 VND total)
meals.dinner: Set menu at a mid-range local restaurant — try ca kho to (caramelized fish in clay pot) with rice and soup (~100,000–150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is a good day to do laundry (many hostels and guesthouses offer laundry service for ~20,000–30,000 VND per kg). Start thinking about any souvenirs you want to buy in the next two days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise walk or jog along the beach one last time. Reflect on the journey so far. Visit any spots you may have missed earlier in the trip — a temple, viewpoint, or local neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse local markets and craft shops for budget-friendly souvenirs: lacquerware, silk scarves, hand-embroidered items, and Vietnamese coffee beans make excellent gifts. Bargain politely for fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Organize a farewell street food crawl with fellow travelers you've met during the trip. Visit 4–5 different street food stalls, ordering small portions at each to maximize variety.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi with a strong ca phe den (black Vietnamese coffee) at a sidewalk cafe (~35,000 VND total)
meals.lunch: Goi cuon (fresh spring rolls) with peanut dipping sauce and a bowl of bun thit nuong (~50,000–65,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl: try nem (fried spring rolls), grilled skewers, banh trang nuong (grilled rice paper pizza), and fresh fruit (~100,000–150,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: When buying souvenirs, compare prices at multiple stalls before purchasing. Avoid buying items made from wildlife or endangered species. Pack purchases carefully to avoid damage during the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take one last stroll along the beach or through a favorite local street. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. Store luggage at reception if your departure is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use remaining local currency on last-minute snacks, drinks, or small souvenirs. Visit any final must-see spots nearby. Head to the airport or bus/train station depending on onward travel plans. Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure day. Reflect on an incredible 10-day budget adventure through Vietnam — the food, the culture, the people, and the memories made.

meals.breakfast: One final bowl of pho or banh mi — a proper Vietnamese farewell meal (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Light snacks from a convenience store or airport food court (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or onboard the flight

day_by_day.notes: Spend remaining VND on food and drinks before departure — it's difficult to exchange small amounts of Vietnamese Dong abroad. Keep a small amount as a memento. Double-check passport, boarding pass, and all belongings before leaving the resort. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour street food stall or hotel room service — try a bowl of pho or banh mi to kick off the culinary adventure.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer with your hotel to avoid stress upon late arrival. Exchange some currency (VND) at the airport for small expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Enjoy the coastal scenery and breathe in the sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood around the resort. Visit a nearby local market to soak in the sights, smells, and sounds of Vietnamese daily life. Pick up fresh tropical fruits and observe vendors in action.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby coastal town strip for dinner and an evening stroll. Explore lit-up streets and find a local restaurant serving fresh seafood — a staple of Vietnam's beachfront regions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café offering Vietnamese-style breakfast: xoi (sticky rice) or banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) with iced ca phe sua da (Vietnamese iced coffee).
meals.lunch: Local market food stall — try com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) for around 40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront seafood restaurant — grilled prawns, steamed clams with lemongrass, and fresh spring rolls. Budget around 150,000–250,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to adjust to the time zone. Download Google Maps offline for Vietnam and get a local SIM card at a nearby phone shop for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient temple, pagoda, or cultural heritage site in the region. Take time to observe local worshippers, admire the architecture, and learn about Vietnamese spiritual traditions. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees).
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a local cooking class or street food walking tour in the nearest town. Learn to make classic dishes like fresh spring rolls, pho broth, or banh xeo (sizzling crepes). This is a hands-on cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and explore the night market or local food street. Sample a variety of street food bites from different vendors.

meals.breakfast: Pho bo (beef noodle soup) at a local pho shop — a classic Vietnamese morning meal. Budget 50,000–80,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class or grab bun bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) at a local eatery.
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl — try banh mi, nem nuong (grilled pork skewers), and fresh coconut. Budget 100,000–150,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance online or through your hotel concierge. Cooking classes typically cost 300,000–600,000 VND and are well worth the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby natural attraction — a national park, waterfall, or scenic viewpoint accessible from the resort area. Hire a local motorbike taxi (xe om) or rent a scooter for authentic backpacker-style exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the natural landscape. If near a national park, hike a short trail. If near the coast, explore hidden coves or snorkel at a local reef. Enjoy the outdoors and take in Vietnam's stunning natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower and refresh. Head out for a relaxed dinner at a mid-range local restaurant with an outdoor terrace.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi from a street cart near the hotel — a classic Vietnamese baguette sandwich with pate, pickled vegetables, and herbs. Budget 25,000–40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a simple roadside quan (eatery) near your natural attraction — try bun thit nuong (grilled pork noodle bowl). Budget 60,000–90,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner — ca kho to (caramelized fish in clay pot) with steamed rice and rau muong xao toi (stir-fried morning glory with garlic). Budget 120,000–200,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have an international driving permit and always wear a helmet. Fuel up before heading to remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local village or artisan community near the resort. Observe traditional crafts such as lantern-making, silk weaving, or pottery. Engage with local artisans and consider purchasing handmade souvenirs directly from makers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historic district or old town on foot. Wander through colonial-era architecture, colorful shop houses, and hidden alleyways. Pop into small galleries or cultural centers to learn about the region's history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese performance if available locally — water puppetry, ca tru (ceremonial singing), or a folk music show. Check with your hotel for scheduled performances.

meals.breakfast: Chao (Vietnamese rice porridge/congee) with ginger and shredded chicken at a local breakfast stall. Budget 40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with shrimp and pork) at a local noodle shop in the historic district. Budget 60,000–90,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the cultural district — set menu with multiple Vietnamese dishes. Budget 180,000–280,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Carry small denominations of VND for artisan purchases and tips. Bargaining is acceptable at markets but always do so respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning — relax on the resort's beachfront, swim, or try a water sport activity such as kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding available near the resort. This is your mid-trip recharge day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local spa or wellness center for a traditional Vietnamese massage or herbal treatment. Many mid-range spas offer 60–90 minute sessions at reasonable prices, perfect for tired backpacker muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset happy hour at a beachfront bar near the resort. Watch the sun dip into the sea with a fresh coconut or a local Bia Hoi (draft beer). Then enjoy a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the spread and fuel up for a relaxed day.
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — goi cuon (fresh spring rolls) and a tropical fruit smoothie from a beachside vendor. Budget 80,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Casual beachfront seafood BBQ restaurant — choose your fresh catch and have it grilled to order. Budget 200,000–300,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa in advance, especially if visiting during a busy period. A 60-minute traditional massage typically costs 150,000–300,000 VND at a reputable local spa.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bicycle ride through the surrounding countryside or coastal roads. Rent bikes from the hotel or a nearby shop and explore rice paddies, fishing villages, or rural scenery at a slow, immersive pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village and interact with fishermen. If timing aligns, watch the morning catch being sorted and sold. Learn about the traditional fishing culture that defines coastal Vietnamese life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town for a street food dinner experience. Seek out a bustling local food street and try dishes you haven't eaten yet — explore boldly.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the bike ride — hu tieu (southern-style clear noodle soup) at a local breakfast spot. Budget 50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at the fishing village — grilled fish wrapped in rice paper with herbs and dipping sauce. Budget 100,000–150,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner adventure — bun dau mam tom (vermicelli with tofu and shrimp paste), oc (snails), and che (sweet dessert soup). Budget 100,000–180,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental typically costs 50,000–100,000 VND per day. Start early to avoid midday heat. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a significant cultural or historical landmark in the broader region — a UNESCO World Heritage Site, ancient citadel, or museum. Hire a local guide for deeper context and storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the landmark or nearby area. Visit a local museum or interpretive center to understand Vietnam's complex history — from ancient kingdoms to the French colonial era and beyond.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a farewell-style dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant — treat yourself to a more refined Vietnamese dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Banh can (mini rice pancakes with quail eggs) or banh beo (steamed rice cakes) — regional specialties. Budget 40,000–70,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Restaurant lunch near the heritage site — com hen (baby clam rice) or bun bo Hue if in the central region. Budget 80,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Vietnamese restaurant — multi-course meal with regional specialties, craft beer or local wine. Budget 250,000–400,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a licensed local guide for heritage sites — they add enormous value and context. Expect to pay 200,000–400,000 VND for a half-day guided tour.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to a vibrant local wet market (cho) — the best time to see it in full swing is before 9am. Watch vendors sell everything from live seafood to exotic herbs, spices, and tropical fruits. Engage with locals and practice a few Vietnamese phrases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for personal exploration, souvenir shopping, or revisiting a favorite spot from earlier in the trip. Browse local handicraft shops for lacquerware, silk scarves, conical hats (non la), or handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with a view — book a rooftop or waterfront restaurant for a memorable last full evening. Reflect on the journey over a delicious Vietnamese meal.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, sticky rice cakes, and Vietnamese drip coffee bought directly from market vendors. Budget 50,000–80,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Banh mi from a famous local spot or a bowl of cao lau (if in Hoi An region) — celebrate your last full day with a beloved dish. Budget 40,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop or waterfront restaurant — Vietnamese fusion or traditional multi-course spread with local rice wine (ruou). Budget 300,000–450,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — lacquerware and ceramics need bubble wrap. Leave room in your luggage for last-minute purchases. Confirm checkout time with Aegean Bliss Resort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take in the sounds of the waves, reflect on the trip, and capture final photos of the stunning Vietnamese coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure time, explore any final spots nearby or relax at a café. Organize luggage and confirm transportation to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport for departure. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before international flights. Use remaining VND on last-minute snacks or airport souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — one last bowl of pho or banh mi with ca phe sua da. Savor every bite. Budget 50,000–80,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the hotel or airport — goi cuon and fresh juice. Budget 80,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure schedule.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some VND aside for airport expenses and tips. Take a final moment to appreciate Vietnam's incredible culture, food, and warmth. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront suite. Enjoy a welcome drink at the resort's lobby lounge.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night light supper at the resort's 24-hour dining service. Unwind on your private balcony with ocean sounds. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Skip or in-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — Vietnamese pho, spring rolls, and tropical fruit platter

day_by_day.notes: Arrival at 22:30 means no sightseeing on Day 1. Focus on a smooth check-in and rest. Confirm resort transfer was pre-arranged. Keep luggage minimal for easy access.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by an orientation walk along the beachfront promenade. Explore the immediate coastal area, take in the scenery, and get acquainted with the local neighborhood surrounding the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural tour of the nearest historic district or village. Visit local temples, pagodas, and artisan markets. Engage with local craftspeople and learn about traditional Vietnamese culture and heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Enjoy a premium Vietnamese fine-dining dinner featuring regional specialties prepared by the resort's executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort breakfast buffet — Vietnamese bánh mì, congee, tropical fruits, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Local upscale restaurant near the resort — grilled seafood, fresh spring rolls, Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.dinner: Resort's signature restaurant — multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recover from jet lag while gently easing into the Vietnamese atmosphere. Request a resort concierge briefing on local customs and upcoming itinerary logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning street food walking tour with a private guide. Explore local markets and street stalls sampling authentic Vietnamese breakfast dishes including bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls), xôi (sticky rice), and cà phê trứng (egg coffee).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a prominent cultural landmark — a UNESCO-listed heritage site, royal citadel, or ancient town nearby. Private guided tour with an expert historian providing in-depth cultural context and storytelling.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or cultural performance. Follow with dinner at a curated fine-dining restaurant known for modern Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour — sampling bánh cuốn, xôi, and egg coffee at local stalls
meals.lunch: Upscale local restaurant — bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup) or cao lầu noodles with premium ingredients
meals.dinner: Award-winning Vietnamese restaurant — chef's tasting menu featuring lacquered duck, lotus root salad, and mango sticky rice dessert

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples and heritage sites. Carry small denominations of Vietnamese Dong for street food vendors. Stay hydrated in the warm climate.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise boat excursion along a scenic river or bay. Enjoy the tranquil morning atmosphere, observe local fishing communities, and capture stunning landscape photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive Vietnamese cooking class at a premium culinary school or resort kitchen. Learn to prepare signature dishes including phở, gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and chè (Vietnamese dessert soup).
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop dining experience at a luxury restaurant with panoramic views. Enjoy craft cocktails and a curated menu blending Vietnamese flavors with international techniques.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the resort before the early boat excursion
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as part of the culinary experience
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine-dining restaurant — pan-seared barramundi, truffle-infused phở consommé, and Vietnamese crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and boat excursion through the resort concierge in advance. Bring sunscreen and a light layer for the morning boat trip. The cooking class is a highlight — take photos throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby natural wonder — limestone karst landscapes, rice terraces, or a national park. Private vehicle and guide provided for a comfortable premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploration of the natural site with a guided trek, kayak excursion, or bamboo boat ride through scenic waterways. Optional visit to a local minority village for cultural exchange.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Indulge in a traditional Vietnamese spa treatment — herbal steam bath, lemongrass massage, or full-body scrub using local ingredients. Quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Vietnamese-style congee, fresh papaya, and strong Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style premium lunch prepared by the resort chef and enjoyed at a scenic outdoor location during the day trip
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront restaurant — grilled tiger prawns, morning glory stir-fry, and coconut pandan cake

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable trekking shoes and bring insect repellent for the nature excursion. The spa should be booked at least a day in advance. This is an ideal recovery and rejuvenation evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a vibrant local market in the nearest city or town. Browse handcrafted silk, lacquerware, conical hats, and artisan goods. Engage with vendors and practice gentle bargaining with guidance from your local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a renowned museum or cultural center — the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology equivalent in the region, a war history site, or a fine arts museum. Private curator-led tour for an enriched experience.
day_by_day.evening: Street food dinner tour through the city's most celebrated food lanes. Sample bún chả (grilled pork noodles), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), nem nướng (grilled pork skewers), and chè ba màu (three-color dessert drink).

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs benedict with Vietnamese pork belly, fresh juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Upscale local eatery — cơm tấm (broken rice) with grilled pork chop, pickled vegetables, and iced Vietnamese coffee
meals.dinner: Curated street food experience across multiple premium street stalls with a private food guide

day_by_day.notes: Bring a reusable bag for market shopping. The street food tour is best experienced with an empty stomach — pace yourself across the multiple stops. Comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to a different Vietnamese destination — either a northern highland region, central heritage city, or southern delta area depending on resort location. Scenic journey by private car or domestic flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the new destination and check in to a pre-arranged luxury day-use hotel or lounge. Explore the immediate area with a local guide — ancient streets, colonial architecture, or riverside promenades.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium cultural dinner show blending traditional music, dance, and regional cuisine. Experience the unique flavors and artistic heritage of the new region.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — light and energizing with Vietnamese fruit, yogurt, and croissants
meals.lunch: En route stop at a highly regarded local restaurant — mì Quảng (turmeric noodles) or hủ tiếu (southern noodle soup)
meals.dinner: Cultural dinner show venue — regional set menu featuring local specialties paired with Vietnamese wines or craft beers

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all transportation logistics with the resort concierge the evening before. Keep a day bag packed for the journey. This travel day is designed to be comfortable and scenic, not rushed.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise visit to an iconic Vietnamese landmark — Hạ Long Bay, Hội An Ancient Town, Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, or Phong Nha caves depending on location. Private guided experience before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive cultural workshop — traditional lantern making in Hội An, silk weaving demonstration, or Vietnamese calligraphy class. Hands-on engagement with local artisans in a premium studio setting.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury river cruise or bay cruise with gourmet dinner on board. Watch the lanterns float on the river or observe the karst mountains at dusk while enjoying a curated Vietnamese seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light grab-and-go breakfast from the hotel before the early sunrise excursion — bánh mì and iced coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside or harbor-view restaurant — white rose dumplings, fried wontons, and cao lầu noodles
meals.dinner: Private gourmet dinner cruise — five-course Vietnamese seafood menu with champagne and sunset views

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise excursion requires a very early start — set alarms accordingly. The dinner cruise is a premium highlight of the trip; dress smart-casual. Book both well in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning with a yoga or tai chi session on the beach or resort grounds led by a private instructor. Follow with a spa breakfast experience — healthy Vietnamese wellness dishes and herbal teas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final cultural exploration — visit a remaining must-see attraction, gallery, or neighborhood. Shop for premium souvenirs including hand-embroidered silk, lacquerware, custom ao dài (traditional dress), or artisan coffee blends.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell premium dining experience at the most celebrated restaurant in the area. Celebrate the journey with a chef's table experience or private dining room reservation featuring the best of Vietnamese haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Spa wellness breakfast — congee with ginger and century egg, green papaya salad, herbal teas, and fresh coconut water
meals.lunch: Casual upscale café — bánh mì with premium fillings, Vietnamese iced coffee, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at a Michelin-recommended or award-winning Vietnamese restaurant — seven-course tasting menu with wine and cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to finalize souvenir shopping and pack acquired items carefully. The farewell dinner is the culinary centerpiece of the trip — make a reservation at least 3–5 days in advance. Reflect on the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast with ocean views. Take a slow walk along the beach, collect memories, and soak in the last moments of Vietnamese coastal beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport or onward destination. Allow ample time for a relaxed, unhurried departure. Optional last-minute stop at a premium café or souvenir boutique near the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days of Vietnamese culture, cuisine, and coastal luxury. Optional airport lounge access for a comfortable pre-flight experience.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — grand farewell breakfast buffet with all Vietnamese favorites: phở, bánh cuốn, tropical fruits, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Airport or departure lounge — light Vietnamese snacks or a premium café meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort if the flight allows. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the night before. Ensure all purchases, especially fragile lacquerware or silk, are properly packed. Keep travel documents and currency exchanged or settled.
